stories.headline: Denver Health CEO accuses city of abandoning decades-long addiction treatment funding commitment
stories.summary:
Denver Health CEO Donna Lynne publicly accused the city of abandoning a more than 50-year funding commitment to Denver CARES, a substance abuse withdrawal management and residential treatment program, describing this year's budget negotiations as "not a good faith negotiation." Lynne clashed with Mayor Mike Johnston over nearly $23 million the health system says it needs from the city, including $3.9 million toward the projected $12.4 million cost of Denver CARES in 2027.

The city failed to fund Denver CARES last year for the first time in five decades, forcing Denver Health to absorb roughly $5 million in costs. Lynne said the health system cannot continue absorbing those costs indefinitely and warned that failure to pay could constitute a material breach of a 1997 operating agreement, potentially allowing Denver Health to stop providing the service.

The dispute surfaced during a formal budget hearing with city officials as Denver Health sought funding omitted from Johnston's proposed 2027 budget. Denver Health has already demonstrated its willingness to confront the city over funding, having previously sent a termination notice over jail medical services before the two sides reached a deal last month.

stories.headline: House Speaker Mike Johnson's PAC contributes $250K to Colorado redistricting ballot measure
stories.summary:
A federal leadership PAC created by U.S. House Speaker Mike Johnson contributed $250,000 to Fair Redistricting Colorado, the issue committee backing Amendment 86, a November ballot measure that would make it harder to redraw congressional district boundaries outside the state's established constitutional process. The American Revival PAC made the contribution in August, making Johnson's committee the largest outside donor to the campaign.

Amendment 86 was crafted by Advance Colorado, a conservative nonprofit that does not disclose its donors, as a direct response to a Democratic-backed redistricting initiative that the Colorado Supreme Court unanimously struck down in June for violating the state constitution's single-subject requirement. The Democratic proposal, backed by money tied to House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, would have redrawn congressional maps in ways analysts said could have flipped three Republican-held seats.

The amendment would require Colorado's Independent Redistricting Commission to reconvene and hold public hearings before any mid-decade congressional map changes take effect, and would require Colorado Supreme Court review and approval. It needs 55% voter support to pass. Democrats have formed an opposition committee, Colorado Draws the Line, but have not yet reported raising or spending any money.

stories.headline: Colorado joins 11 other states in settling Paramount-Warner Bros. merger lawsuit
stories.summary:
Colorado and 11 other states reached a settlement Monday with Paramount over its $81 billion acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery, clearing a major legal hurdle for a deal that would combine studios, networks including CBS and CNN, and streaming platforms HBO Max and Paramount+. The Writers Guild of America separately settled its own antitrust challenge the same day.

Under the terms of the agreement, Paramount pledged to increase U.S. film production, establish a fund to support workers displaced by the merger, and implement monitoring of editorial independence at its news operations. The settlement still requires final judicial approval.

Colorado Attorney General Phil Weiser said the settlement "will protect moviegoers and producers" and that his office will continue to monitor the company's commitments. California AG Rob Bonta, who led the state coalition, emphasized that the resolution was not an endorsement of the merger, saying he still opposed the combination of two of Hollywood's largest studios.

stories.headline: University of Colorado system to sell Uptown headquarters, relocate to downtown Independence Plaza
stories.summary:
The University of Colorado system announced it will sell its 115,000-square-foot headquarters building at 1800 Grant St. in Denver's Uptown neighborhood and move administrative operations to Independence Plaza, a 25-story tower at 1050 17th St. in downtown Denver. CU purchased the building in 2006 for $14 million and described it as underutilized; no asking price was disclosed.

The system bought Independence Plaza in August for $28 million, primarily for use by CU Denver. The relocated headquarters will occupy less square footage than the current building, consistent with a hybrid work model in which more than 600 administrative employees split time between office and remote work.

CU officials said the move will provide better office space, improved security, and greater employee access to restaurants and public transit. The system expects to complete the relocation next year.

stories.headline: Edible Beats to open new LoHi restaurant Pip Food + Drink this fall
stories.summary:
Edible Beats, the employee-owned restaurant group behind Linger, El Five, Vital Root and Root Down, announced plans to open a new restaurant called Pip Food + Drink at 2930 Umatilla St. in LoHi, the former location of Sushi Ronin. The restaurant is described as a sister concept to El Five and is expected to open this fall.

The menu will be developed by El Five Executive Chef Corey Ferguson and will feature smaller plates, "micro-cocktails," full entrées, and service spanning lunch, happy hour and dinner. Founder Justin Cucci described the concept as "unexpected and new" within the Edible Beats portfolio, with design inspired by his personal collection of objects.

Separately, Fox Restaurant Concepts announced its upscale restaurant The Henry will open in Cherry Creek North at 201 Fillmore on Dec. 16, marking the brand's first Colorado location. The Henry has existing locations in Los Angeles, Miami, Dallas and Phoenix and will occupy more than 8,500 square feet of ground-floor space, with a companion bar called Hank's Neighborhood Bar to follow.

stories.headline: Colorado ski industry lobbies Senate to reject permanent daylight saving time bill
stories.summary:
Five resort trade groups and two resort companies representing 115 ski areas across 10 states, including Colorado Ski Country, sent a letter to 19 U.S. senators urging rejection of the Sunshine Protection Act of 2026, which passed the House in July on a 308-117 vote. The industry argues that permanent daylight saving time would push winter sunrises past 8 a.m. in Colorado and later than 9 a.m. at western resorts, creating safety hazards for ski patrollers, lift mechanics, snowmakers and groomers who work before dawn.

Resort operators contend that a later sunrise would either force dangerous pre-dawn operations or delay lift-loading until sunlight is available, potentially shortening operating hours and cutting the equivalent of two weeks from the ski season. The industry argues that a morning hour and a late-afternoon hour are not economically interchangeable, as morning hours are when critical avalanche mitigation, lift inspection and run preparation take place.

Alterra Mountain Co. and Powdr joined the trade groups in the lobbying effort. Supporters of the bill, including its House sponsors, cite polls showing that only 12% of Americans favor the current twice-yearly clock change, and argue that year-round daylight saving time improves public safety and economic activity.

stories.headline: Broncos RBs Dobbins, Harvey both potential returnees for Rams game after hamstring injuries
stories.summary:
Head coach Sean Payton indicated Monday that running backs J.K. Dobbins and RJ Harvey both have a chance to play Sunday night when Denver hosts the Los Angeles Rams at Empower Field, following a Week 2 victory over Jacksonville in which rookie Jonah Coleman provided the decisive offensive contribution. Harvey missed the Jacksonville game entirely after injuring his hamstring in Week 1, while Dobbins started but left in the second half with what Payton described as a hamstring issue.

Payton said all three backs — Dobbins, Harvey and Coleman — are capable of serving as featured runners, and called potential availability of the injured pair "a good problem to have." Harvey had been a limited practice participant late last week before the Jacksonville game, suggesting he was not far from a return.

Payton also disclosed Monday that he is managing an L4/L5 vertebrae injury that flares up during game days when he stands for extended periods, causing radiating back pain. He said a recent epidural has helped with pain management and that he does not expect to need surgery during the season.

stories.headline: Avalanche defenseman Brent Burns targeting all-time NHL ironman record this season
stories.summary:
Colorado Avalanche defenseman Brent Burns is setting his sights on the NHL's all-time consecutive games played record as the 2026-27 season approaches, according to reporting cited in a Sports Illustrated roundup of Avalanche news. Burns, a veteran offensive defenseman, would need to continue his streak throughout the coming season to mount a serious challenge at the historic mark.

The Avalanche also generated trade speculation involving goaltender MacKenzie Blackwood, with reports suggesting Blackwood's performance may affect discussions around a potential Connor Hellebuyck trade. Colorado opens training camp with an emphasis on building depth around its core of star players.

The ironman pursuit adds a compelling individual storyline to the Avalanche's season outlook as the team aims to contend for a Stanley Cup after falling short in recent playoff runs.

stories.headline: Two people critically injured in targeted shooting near Loveland I-25 interchange
stories.summary:
Loveland police responded just after midnight Monday to reports of a traffic crash near the I-25 and Eisenhower Boulevard off-ramp and found two people in a single vehicle suffering from gunshot wounds. Both victims were transported to a hospital and remained in critical condition as of Monday morning.

Investigators believe the shooting occurred near the crash scene and that the incident was a targeted attack rather than a random act of violence. No other vehicle was found at the scene, and police said there is no indication of a broader threat to the community.

The Loveland Police Department is leading the investigation and is asking anyone who observed suspicious activity along the I-25 corridor between Crossroads Boulevard and Eisenhower Boulevard around midnight to contact the LPD tip line at (970) 962-2032 or Crime Stoppers at (970) 221-6868.

stories.headline: Denver reports first human West Nile virus case of 2026, later in season than typical
stories.summary:
Denver health officials confirmed Monday the city's first human case of West Nile virus this year, arriving later than the typical August milestone. Colorado has recorded 40 cases statewide so far in 2026, with two deaths and 20 hospitalizations — a relatively low count compared to recent years, which have ranged from 35 cases in 2020 to 634 in 2023.

Jefferson County recorded Colorado's first case of the year in early June, indicating the virus had been circulating in the mosquito population for months before Denver's first confirmed infection. Health officials noted that the majority of infected people have no symptoms, and many who do feel ill never seek testing because the virus resembles influenza.

Mosquito activity this year was elevated by a warm winter and hot summer, though officials noted that mosquito population size does not always correlate directly with West Nile infection rates, which also depend on the amount of virus circulating in local bird populations. Activity is expected to slow as evening temperatures drop and will cease with the season's first hard freeze.

stories.headline: Bear scooped into garbage truck in Castle Rock as statewide encounters hit record levels
stories.summary:
A black bear that had climbed into a dumpster in Castle Rock was picked up and emptied into a Waste Management garbage truck last week, according to a local resident who shared a video of the incident on social media. The bear eventually climbed down from the truck and was scared off by employees of a nearby business, according to witness Evan Elmore.

The incident reflects a dramatic surge in bear activity across Colorado driven by an ongoing drought that has depleted natural food sources. Colorado Parks and Wildlife has responded to 10 bear attacks so far this year — a record — and received 8,672 reports of bear sightings and conflicts between January and August, more than double the same period in 2025 and more than three times the five-year average.

As of early September, 294 black bears had been euthanized in Colorado this year and 98 relocated, more than triple the figures for all of 2025. Wildlife officials said the spike is compounded by hyperphagia, the late-summer and fall period when bears spend up to 20 hours a day foraging to build fat reserves before winter, historically the most conflict-prone time of year.

stories.headline: Eastbound I-70 at Kipling Street to close 83 hours beginning Friday for bridge deck repairs
stories.summary:
The Colorado Department of Transportation announced that eastbound Interstate 70 at Kipling Street will close for 83 hours beginning at 7 p.m. Friday to allow crews to complete bridge deck repairs, concrete work, paving and striping. The closure is scheduled to run through 6 a.m. Tuesday, with traffic routed through the Kipling Street interchange using on- and off-ramps.

Drivers will be unable to enter or exit I-70 at Kipling Street for the duration of the closure, and CDOT warned to expect delays of 30 minutes or longer. The closure follows the completion of westbound I-70 bridge deck repairs at the same location, which finished ahead of schedule, with that roadway reopening around 1 a.m. Monday.

If weather or unforeseen circumstances delay construction, the work will be rescheduled for the following weekend, Oct. 2 through Oct. 6. Motorists are advised to plan alternate routes. Real-time road conditions are available at COtrip.org.
